text:
lena: idea — progressive activation throttle for runtime flags. not just a flat cap: a rolling-window semaphore that widens with successful activations and tightens on errors. prevents sudden cohort-wide flips and quota shock.

josh: can you contrast that with a token-bucket? curious on complexity tradeoffs.
lena: token-bucket is simpler but stateless. progressive window tracks recent successful activations+failures per-cohort and adjusts allowed rate. softer to bursts that are healthy, stricter when errors or quota pressure shows up.
ravi: runtime enforcement or central? centralized checks add latency; local caches avoid RPC storm. maybe hybrid: local fast-path + periodic reconciliation with control plane.
priya: we should also think cross-cohort accounting — if cohort A is throttled and traffic spills to B, we could cascade issues. need a global quota leash or routing fallback.

maya: UX: Console needs an "Override request" flow rather than an instant force-enable. Request creates an audit entry, requires owner approval + 2FA, and shows TTL. Also surface why the throttle fired (e.g., quota pressure vs error spike).
devon: Ops/alerts: SLIs = config.allowed_rate, config.actual_activations, config.throttled_events, config.spillover_routed. Suggest alert when throttled_events > 10 in 2m AND spillover_routed > 0.
cara: SRE: default modes: conservative (fail-closed) for infra-facing flags, permissive (fail-open) for user-experience flags. Emergency safemode for oncall with ephemeral bypass tokens that auto-expire and are logged.
josh: Implementation proposal: implement local rolling-window counter with atomic ops per runtime instance. When window limit hit, runtime returns 429 + Retry-After. Periodic delta-sync with central service to update cohort budgets.
lena: also want preflight to enforce telemetry wiring. If a flag enables a semaphore/rolling-window it must create or attach to a dashboard and have blocked/throttle metrics. preflight should either auto-create dashboards or fail.
configbot: preflight-check: schema OK. WARNING: telemetry bindings missing (config.throttled_events, config.spillover_routed). Recommend auto-provisioning dashboards: /dashboards/flags/1761213141.
priya: can configbot auto-provision an alert stub too? that would help reduce human error.
ravi: +1. we can have a template alert that teams customize. Default thresholds as Devon recommended.
maya: Console detail: timeline view with three lanes — activations, errors, and throttle events. Provide export button to attach to RFC or incident.
devon: also suggest a "dry-run mode" in Console where the mechanism logs what it would have throttled without actually returning 429s. Helpful for rollouts.
cara: runbook: steps to handle a throttled spike: 1) check timeline and spillover; 2) evaluate override request queue; 3) consider circuit-fallback to lower-cost model; 4) open incident if infra flag impacted.
josh: perf considerations: per-request check should be <200ns ideally. Use relaxed atomic counters + sample windows to avoid cache-line thrashing. need microbench.
lena: security: overrides require owner + 2FA + an explanation field stored in audit. auto-revoke after TTL. Also a "review overrides" weekly report to product and security.
priya: product ask: make messages PM-friendly. Console copy should explain in plain English what happened and a one-click link to request an override.
ravi: edge-case: what if the central reconciliation is down and local nodes diverge? we fall back to local conservative view and push alerts. define fail-open vs fail-closed policy per flag at creation time.
lena: action items: lena -> write short RFC and include sample rolling-window config; josh -> perf microbench + implementation sketch; devon -> alert templates; cara -> safemode & runbook; maya -> Console mocks and user copy; priya -> coordinate product copy and PM signoff.
configbot: reminder: create RFC under /eng/flags/rfcs and attach preflight id 1761213141.
lena: thanks all — will demo PoC next week :rocket:
